@liggitt @aojea @xuzhenglun I just analyzed it again. It seems that the reason is this
When the node changes from notready to ready, the controller-manager removes the noschedule and noexecute taints normally (due to the modification of #113136, the controller-manager patch taints have no race). Because other client patch nodes have races, the noshedule taint is patched back. Originally, the node controller watched the node update event and could continue to clear the taint. However, because outdated data (without the no schedule taint) was obtained from the apiserver cache, the noschedule taint on the node was not finally cleared.
So I think this modification is necessary

It looks like the behavior should be like this.

I just ran into a similar issue - part of why this was a problem for me is that I was expecting the taint list to be listType=map so that multiple controllers could use server side apply without clobbering each others changes.

Is there a reason that the node taint list is currently set to atomic? This behaviour requires each controller to respect each others changes when forming patches, which helps lead to this race condition. It also makes SSA unusable unless always forcing taint changes.

/sig node

Is there a way to reproduce it without adding a sleep? I assume you encountered this issue in a production or test environment. Could you describe your use case?

> /sig node
> 
> Is there a way to reproduce it without adding a sleep? I assume you encountered this issue in a production or test environment. Could you describe your use case?

Yes. If there are multiple kube-apiserver instances in the cluster, there will be problems in the following scenarios:
When the node status changes from not ready to ready, the two goroutines of kube-controller-manager that remove the unreachable noschedule taint and noexecute taint update the taint information at the same time, which may cause overwriting. When the noschedule taint is deleted and overwritten again, when processing subsequent node change messages, the node-controller will load balance to a random apiserver to obtain the latest node information, but may access a node that has only updated the removal of the noschedule taint, causing the node-controller to think that the noschedule taint has been removed and no longer process it.
The result is that when the node status changes to ready, the noschedule taint is still retained.

Technically, this makes sense, but the interval at which `monitorNodeHealth` runs is determined by the `--node-monitor-period` parameter of the `kube-controller-manager`. By default, it runs every 5 seconds, which I believe is sufficient to balance the Apiserver cache and etcd. 
ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0f095cf0ba5156a972b446a5f65c963fe2a7919c/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L508-L513

If you encountered this issue, you might need to provide more detailed information about your environment configuration when the issue occurred :)

> Technically, this makes sense, but the interval at which `monitorNodeHealth` runs is determined by the `--node-monitor-period` parameter of the `kube-controller-manager`. By default, it runs every 5 seconds, which I believe is sufficient to balance the Apiserver cache and etcd. ref:
> 
> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0f095cf0ba5156a972b446a5f65c963fe2a7919c/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L508-L513
> 
> If you encountered this issue, you might need to provide more detailed information about your environment configuration when the issue occurred :)

This has nothing to do with the interval at which monitorNodeHealth runs. The main problem is that the processing of the taint no execute and no schedule is handled by two goroutines. In addition, the TaintManager processes node events triggered by watch, not controlled by the --node-monitor-period parameter.

The cause analysis is wrong. The current patch taints operation should not cause overwriting. I will continue to study it.
/close

review_comments: is this firstTry not enough to avoid the race?

Yes. there will be problems in the following scenarios:
When the node status changes from not ready to ready, the two goroutines of kube-controller-manager that remove the unreachable noschedule taint and noexecute taint update the taint information at the same time, which may cause overwriting.

Even if the node-controller watches the changes of the node, if in a scenario with multiple kube-apiservers, if the old data (without the noschedule taint, the real data is that the noschedule taint has been overwritten) is obtained from the kube-apiserver, the result is that when the node status changes to ready, the noschedule taint is still retained.

Can you explain why the original code can race? 

In the original behavior, In my understanding, the `resourceVersion` in node acts as an a optimistic lock to avoid race. so no matter getting a stale node object in the first try or patching node by another client in the same time, both will leads a conflict error to avoid race.

As the picture above can see, the latest version of the node is `1576187`. When I do patch to modify taint with a stale version `1575874`, an conflict error occureded. And when I do the same thing with the right version `1576187`, patching is successed.

If the experiment I did was right, IMO, removing `resourceVersion=0` will not make any difference.
